title: mbolt (PyPI 0.1.0, github doramirdor/mbolt): profile-guided co-activation layout for GGUF MoE + explicit-read prefetch
setting: Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B (33 GB file, 512 experts/layer), Apple M5 Pro MacBook, CPU experts, Apple SSD, medians of 3 runs; baseline stock file + stock llama.cpp (mmap)
headline: README table: stock 5.80 tok/s; stock file+prefetcher 7.60 (1.31x); reorder+prefetcher 8.00 (1.38x); interleave(gate/up/down contiguous)+prefetcher 9.00 (1.55x); 32 GB squeeze 9.80 vs 6.00 stock (1.63x); reads/token 1418 -> ~370 (2.23x), avg read 450 KB -> 1.5 MB
caveat: The PyPI page failed to load; numbers read from the GitHub README. Most of the gain is the prefetcher (1.31x) and the interleave (gate/up/down contiguous); pure co-activation reorder adds 8.00/7.60 = 1.05x over prefetcher alone, matching our 1.045x. README itself says gains need an I/O-bound regime, only help with explicit reads (mmap parity), shrink with LRU caching and large slices. Self-reported, 8 stars, one machine, 33 GB model on a machine with more RAM (squeezed).
notes: Closest published work to the family and uses a 512-expert model like ours. README also cites an independent MLX cross-check (+9.7% to +32% decode, 1.29-2.34x I/O) not verified by us. Layout trained on general data gave 1.22x on code (cross-domain transfer reported).

title: LLM in a flash: Efficient Large Language Model Inference with Limited Memory (Alizadeh et al., Apple; arXiv 2312.11514 v3, ACL 2024, submitted Dec 2023)
setting: OPT 6.7B, Falcon 7B (ReLU), Phi-2, Persimmon 8B, Llama 2 7B (FATReLU); Apple M1 Max, M2 Ultra, RTX 4090; model given ~half its size in DRAM; baselines naive and hybrid loading
headline: Table 2 (OPT 6.7B I/O): predictor+hybrid 738 ms @1.25 GB/s, +windowing 164 ms, +row-column bundling 87 ms @2.25 GB/s. Table 3: OPT 6.7B CPU 3182 -> 669 ms/token, Metal M1 2389 -> 565, GPU 2218 -> 84
caveat: The PDF url returned binary; read via arxiv.org/html and abs. Dense ReLU-sparse FFN neurons, not experts; baseline numbers are best-case theory. Appendix D negative result (co-activation bundling with closest friend, hot neurons loaded repeatedly) confirmed from html and a mirror.
notes: Row-column bundling is the analogue of our gate/up/down repack (family #19), not of co-activation reorder. 4-5x CPU headline is vs naive load-everything.

title: MoE-Infinity: Efficient MoE Inference on Personal Machines with Sparsity-Aware Expert Cache (Xue et al., Edinburgh; arXiv 2401.14361 v3, Mar 2025)
setting: Switch-128, NLLB-128, DeepSeek-V2-Lite, Arctic, Mixtral-8x7B; single RTX A5000 24 GB, PCIe 4.0, host DRAM 32 GB to 1 TB; batch 1, prompt 512, decode 32; baselines DeepSpeed, llama.cpp(Ollama), Mixtral-Offloading, BrainStorm, vLLM
headline: Abstract 3.1-16.7x per-token latency (conclusion says 2.7-13.7x). Table 1 DeepSeek-V2-Lite TPOT: MoE-Infinity 155 ms, vLLM 485, DeepSpeed 737, Mixtral-Offloading 1250, Ollama 2590 ms
caveat: Catalog says 2-20x; paper says 3.1-16.7x (abstract) / 2.7-13.7x (conclusion). All experts stay in host DRAM; GPU cache; no SSD, no disk layout. Transfer is DRAM->GPU, not NVMe->CPU.
notes: Request-level activation-matrix caching; useful as cache-policy prior art only.

title: MoE-SpeQ: Speculative Quantized Decoding with Proactive Expert Prefetching and Offloading for MoE (arXiv 2511.14102 v1, 18 Nov 2025); v3 renamed 'Specter: Fast MoE Inference via Quantization-Enabled Multi-Step Speculative Offloading', ASPLOS '27
setting: v1 abstract: Phi-MoE, 'memory-constrained devices'. v3 full text: Phi-3.5-MoE (41.9B), Qwen1.5-MoE, DeepSeekV2-Lite with GPTQ INT4 draft; one A100 40 GB, Xeon, 256 GB RAM, PCIe 4.0 x16; baselines vLLM, HF, llama.cpp, Mixtral-Offloading, SpecMoEOff
headline: v1 abstract: up to 2.34x over a state-of-the-art offloading framework on Phi-MoE. v3: average 1.50x TPOT (up to 1.88x) over SpecMoEOff at batch 1; up to 6.02x at batch 32 on DeepSeekV2-Lite
caveat: 2.34x appears in the v1 abstract only; I did not find it in the first 100k characters of v3 (rest unread), so figure belongs to the older version. GPU with PCIe from DRAM, not NVMe to CPU. Draft is a quantized copy of the target on the GPU; gain is prefetch overlap, not fewer bytes. Catalog title is stale (paper was renamed).
notes: Full-text v3 not completely read (39k chars unread).

title: Efficient Mixture-of-Experts LLM Inference with Apple Silicon NPUs (NPUMoE; Benazir and Lin; arXiv 2604.18788, 22 Apr 2026)
setting: Phi-3.5-MoE (83.75 GB), Phi-tiny-MoE, Qwen3-30B-A3B; M2 Max 64 GB and M2 Ultra 192 GB; baselines Core ML CPU, Core ML naive, ANEMLL; whole model resident in RAM
headline: Prefill latency 1.32x-5.55x lower across baselines (e.g. 2.07x vs Core ML CPU at prompt 1024, chunk 256); energy 1.81x-7.37x; calibration predicts dominant experts with 86% (top-4) and 94% (top-8) mean overlap in prefill (65.2% prefill / 77.0% decode across datasets); 'Ours-base' (NPU, one graph per expert) is worst, full system 2.89x faster than it
caveat: No disk streaming; models fit in unified memory so prefill is compute/dispatch-bound, the opposite of our I/O-bound regime. Gains are vs CPU-only Core ML, not vs a tuned llama.cpp. GPU is 1.26x-5.4x faster than NPU (appendix) with higher energy.
notes: Final 3k chars unread. Supports the break-even logic: NPU helps only when prefill is compute-bound.

title: ProMoE: Fast MoE-based LLM Serving using Proactive Caching (Song, Zhong, Chen, Chen; arXiv 2410.22134 v3)
setting: DeepSeek-MoE, DeepSeek-V2-Lite, Qwen1.5-MoE, Qwen2-MoE (INT4), Mixtral-8x7B (INT4); RTX 4090 24 GB, i9-14900K, 128 GB DRAM, PCIe 4.0 (23.9 GB/s measured); transformers and llama.cpp baselines; batch 1 default (1-4 tested)
headline: vs offloading baselines: avg 2.20x prefill (up to 3.21x), 2.07x decode (up to 5.02x); vs hand-crafted caches: 1.78x prefill, 1.34x decode
caveat: PDF unreadable; read from arxiv.org/html. Experts live in DRAM and move over PCIe to a GPU; no disk. Paper notes llama.cpp CPU offload beats it for Mixtral decode. Prefill speedups come from overlap, which we already assume.

title: DuoServe-MoE: Dual-Phase Expert Prefetch and Cache Scheduling for Efficient MoE LLM Inference (Zhang et al., Univ. of Sydney; arXiv 2509.07379 v1, 9 Sep 2025)
setting: 4-bit AWQ Mixtral-8x7B and 8x22B on vLLM; RTX A5000 24 GB or A6000 48 GB, 128 GB RAM, PCIe 4.0; baselines Accelerate and MoESys reimplemented; single request
headline: End-to-end latency 1.42x-7.54x, TTFT 1.78x-3.8x, decode throughput 1.78x-7.04x; predictor Table 3 top-2 hit 54-67%, at-least-one hit 90-95%
caveat: GPU, 8 experts top-2, experts in host RAM. Prefill: tokens grouped by expert so each expert loads once, 2-expert GPU cache with compute/communication streams. Dense prefill activation claim holds there because Mixtral top-2 of 8.
notes: Supports 'prefill touches nearly all experts' only for 8-expert models; our own trace shows 55-66% coverage after 200 tokens on 128 experts.

title: ssd-llm (github quantumnic/ssd-llm): run 70B+ LLMs on Apple Silicon using SSD as extended memory
setting: Rust, macOS Metal, 16-36 GB Macs; README table for LLaMA 7B/13B/70B Q4_0 lists only layer-load ms (2/4/8 ms per layer) with 'TBD' tok/s
headline: No measured throughput. Layer-major prompt processing (each layer loaded once for all prompt tokens) is listed as a feature; roadmap lists it under v0.6
caveat: No benchmark, 58 stars, 65 commits, dense models mostly; unclear whether layer-major prefill is implemented or planned. Evidence only that the idea is published as a design, not that it works.
notes: MIT license. Claims of 2-3x speculative speedup unbacked.

title: Deltafin: 2.8T Kimi K3 from Four SSDs on a MacBook: Layer Streaming as a Local Inference Lever (contextstudios.ai blog, published 2026-09-23, benchmarks 2026-09-08)
setting: MacBook Pro M5 Max 128 GB, four NVMe SSDs, Kimi K3 (2.8T, 1.45 TB expert weights), argonautlabsai/deltafin fork; single cold run per setting
headline: Decode 0.92-1.13 tok/s (512-token response 0.92 off / 1.00 drafter on; 128-token 0.93 / 1.13); TTFT 6.3 min for a 512-token prompt, same with drafter on or off; SSD scaling 52/73/90/100% (percentages only)
caveat: Catalog URL is truncated (ends '-layer') and returns 404; the working URL ends '-layer-streaming'. Blog is secondary, author unnamed, runs a single cold run each. The blog's own diagnosis is that prefill re-reads each layer's experts eight times and a fix is not built, so 6.3 min is not a layer-major prefill; it shows the penalty of NOT doing it. Hardware is far beyond our 8-32 GB.
notes: Drafter helped decode 1.08x-1.22x on a 128 GB machine; speculative gain seen only with large RAM cache.

title: FluxMoE: Decoupling Expert Residency for High-Performance MoE Serving (Liu et al.; arXiv 2604.02715 v1, 3 Apr 2026)
setting: Mixtral-8x7B (94 GB) and Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B (160 GB), vLLM v0.10.2; 4x NVIDIA L40 48 GB, Xeon 8358, 2 TiB DRAM; baselines vLLM, vLLM-O (offload last 12.5% layers)
headline: Qwen3-Next batch 256, 4096 ctx: up to 3.0x vs vLLM and 3.7x vs vLLM-O; at batch 32 only 63.9% of vLLM throughput; PagedTensor overhead <=3.0%
caveat: 'Storage hierarchy' here is a lossless Huffman-compressed GPU backend (~20% smaller, BF16) plus pinned host DRAM; I found no NVMe streaming in the part read (last 18k chars unread). Datacenter GPUs, large batch; frees VRAM for KV cache.
notes: Not a disk-streaming system; catalog wording overstates.

title: InstInfer: In-Storage Attention Offloading for Cost-Effective Long-Context LLM Inference (Pan et al.; arXiv 2409.04992 v1, 8 Sep 2024)
setting: OPT-13B (LLaMA-2-7B for accuracy); A6000 48 GB, Xeon 5320, 96 GB DDR4; CSD prototype on Zynq-7045 / OpenSSD ZU17EG, 8 flash channels at 1.4 GB/s each; baselines DeepSpeed, FlexGen, FlexGen-SparQ
headline: Up to 11.1x throughput over FlexGen; data migration cut up to 94.0%; 6.85x vs FlexGen at batch 64; Table I FPGA use 85% DSP on Zynq-7045
caveat: Offloads attention and KV, not weights; dense 13B, batch up to 256, GPU host. The paper's own compute figure (CSD 2-3 orders of magnitude weaker than a GPU, from search snippet) argues against expert GEMV in a drive. Page read to 100k of 112k chars.
notes: Only evidence that CSD FPGA can do real decode work, and only for attention.

title: HillInfer: Efficient Long-Context LLM Inference on the Edge with Hierarchical KV Eviction using SmartSSD (He Sun et al.; arXiv 2602.18750 v1, 21 Feb 2026)
setting: LongChat 7B, LLaMA 13B, Qwen-7B, OPT-6.7B; RTX 4090 24 GB, Xeon 8352V, 64 GB, Samsung SmartSSD (Xilinx UltraScale+, 4 GB DDR4, 4 TB NAND), batch 8
headline: Up to 8.56x speedup (4.21-8.56x), latency down 76.25%-88.32% on LongBench; SmartSSD peak bandwidth about 4 GB/s
caveat: Paper says limited SSD bandwidth makes KV transfer dominate (Fig. 3) which is about KV, not weights; the catalog's 'bandwidth remains the bottleneck even with in-storage compute' is an interpretation. The 4 GB/s SmartSSD figure is at least a data point on a real CSD's ceiling. Setup section inconsistent with motivation section (RTX 3080 vs 4090).
notes: Only real SmartSSD LLM use found; quantitative results are in figures only.

title: Conduit: Programmer-Transparent Near-Data Processing Using Multiple Compute-Capable Resources in SSDs (Nadig ... Mutlu; arXiv 2601.17633 v1, Jan 2026)
setting: In-house simulator on MQSim + Ramulator 2 + QEMU, 2 TB SSD 8 channels, real Xeon and A100 hosts; six data-intensive apps incl. LLM inference/training; baselines ISP, PuD-SSD, Flash-Cosmos, Ares-Flash, BW- and DM-Offloading
headline: 1.8x over best prior offloading policy (DM-Offloading), 46% less energy, 3.77 us runtime overhead; DM-Offloading is 2.5x (up to 4.6x on LLM) short of Ideal
caveat: Simulation; I read about half (100k of 198k chars) and saw no MoE or GEMV throughput. Not evidence for expert GEMV in storage.

title: Samsung Electronics Develops Second-Generation SmartSSD (BusinessWire, 20 Jul 2022)
setting: Product press release; AMD Versal Prime VM1802, E3 form factor, PCIe Gen4 x4 (from secondary sources)
headline: Press release (via search summaries, not opened): scan-heavy database queries >50% less time, energy up to 70% lower, CPU use up to 97% lower; no GEMV/GFLOPS figures
caveat: businesswire.com returned 403 and news.samsung.com timed out, so unverified from the primary source; numbers above come from search-result summaries. TechRadar 2025 says the SmartSSD has largely vanished from Samsung's lineup (opinion, not Samsung statement); sold under AMD Xilinx brand.
notes: Enterprise E3 module, no consumer or laptop availability.

title: Containerized In-Storage Processing and Computing-Enabled SSD Disaggregation (DockerSSD; Kwon ... Jung; arXiv 2506.06769 v1, 7 Jun 2025; extended IEEE Micro paper)
setting: FPGA prototype with six RISC-V cores plus gem5 / cycle-accurate SSD simulation; LLM workloads are 8 dense models (137B-1T) as distributed inference on 16-128 DockerSSD pools via TorchServe
headline: 7.9x LLM inference gain (D-Cache vs H-Cache); up to 2.0x on I/O-intensive apps (1.3x vs host in intro); D-Cache 4.6K x faster than D-NoCache
caveat: Now opened (catalog said unopened). Simulated, dense models, pools of up to 128 drives, cache-vs-no-cache baselines with absurd ratios (4.6K x); no MoE, no laptop. Does not support the family.
